title: On Saddle Point Avoidance and Stationary Distribution of Sharpness-Aware Minimization

problem.claim: The work examines the behavior and theoretical properties of Sharpness-Aware Minimization and its unnormalized variant in neural-network training.

contributions.claim: Deterministic USAM is shown to converge to a local minimum and exhibit local acceleration relative to standard gradient descent.
The work characterizes a trade-off between convergence and saddle-point escape for SAM.
The work models USAM as a Markov chain under stationary noise and compares its stationary-distribution objective values with SGD.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report numerical experiments supporting all of their theoretical results.

narrative_sequence.summary: SAM and USAM are widely used in neural-network training.
The authors introduce three theoretical results about (U)SAM.
Deterministic USAM is proved to converge to a local minimum and achieve local acceleration over gradient descent.
SAM's convergence and saddle-point-escape behavior are analyzed as a trade-off.
Under stationary noise, USAM is described as a Markov chain whose stationary-distribution objective values are lower than those achieved by SGD.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports a trade-off between convergence and escaping saddle points.

interpretation.claim: Optimization behavior should be evaluated across both convergence and saddle-point escape rather than by a single criterion.

application.claim: When comparing optimization methods, assess convergence and saddle-point escape jointly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the trade-off occurs.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports lower objective values for USAM than SGD on a stationary distribution under stationary noise.

interpretation.claim: Noise-aware stationary behavior may be relevant when evaluating optimization methods.

application.claim: For noisy optimization settings, compare methods using stationary-distribution behavior as well as convergence metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not define the noise model or the scope of the comparison.

unknowns: Proof assumptions and technical conditions are not provided.
Numerical experiment designs, datasets, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The specific cases in which SAM may fail to converge are not described.
